item.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island, oil prices rise as fears of renewed conflict and disruptions mount
item.description: The US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island have pushed oil prices up 0.5% in early Asian trading. The attacks have revived concerns over an escalation of the conflict and prolonged disruption to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Prabhakar Jha
item.content:encoded: Oil prices rose in early Asian trading on Tuesday after the United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island, reviving fears of an escalation of the conflict and prolonged disruptions to energy supplies from the Middle East.According to a Reuters report, Brent crude futures gained 48 cents, or 0.5%, to $105.25 a barrel by 0104 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 47 cents, or 0.5%, to $96.93 a barrel.The United States carried out strikes on Qeshm Island on Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing American officials. The attacks were described as "defensive measures intended to prevent Iran from targeting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz".The strikes were part of a series of limited US attacks on Iran in recent weeks that Washington has not publicly announced, the Journal reported. The administration has reportedly sought to keep the operations low-profile to avoid signalling a return to large-scale military action.Qeshm Island, located near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, hosts an underground missile site, a naval base and a major desalination plant. The US had also targeted the island during earlier phases of the conflict as well.Oil prices regain risk premium after US strikesBrent crude had settled 7.63% lower, or $8.66, at $104.77 a barrel on Monday. The benchmark had ended October at its highest level in six months amid concerns that the Middle East conflict could escalate after the US midterm elections.The conflict, which began in late February, has reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway earlier handled about a fifth of global crude oil and natural gas supplies.Donald Trump plays down prospect of renewed warUS President Donald Trump downplayed the possibility of a return to full-scale conflict with Iran. Asked on Monday whether he was considering fresh attacks after the midterm elections, Trump said “no”.Trump also said a deal with Tehran remained possible, while Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said that the next move rested with Washington. Iranian officials have warned that the country would retaliate if the US reignited the conflict.Meanwhile, contacts between the two countries are continuing following discussions involving Qatari mediators, according to Reuters. The talks have not yet produced a breakthrough.

item.title: Learjet May Have Broken Up Before Fatal Florida Crash, NTSB Says
item.description: US air safety investigators said there are early indications the Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach, Florida, on Sunday had broken up before impacting the ground, killing all nine people on board and injuring at least one person on the ground.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- US air safety investigators said there are early indications the Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach, Florida, on Sunday had broken up before impacting the ground, killing all nine people on board and injuring at least one person on the ground. “We’re still seeking to determine that,” National Transportation Safety Board Member Tom Chapman told reporters in Florida on Monday when asked if the aircraft’s horizontal stabilizer had come off before the crash, as was indicated by some social media posts. Adverse weather conditions are also a major focus of the investigation, Chapman added. He said the pilots reported experiencing moderate turbulence and icing to air traffic controllers. The pilots then asked to climb, before beginning a rapid descent and transmitting over the radio the aircraft was in an “overspeed condition,” he said. “We’re going to crash into the ground,” an unidentified pilot can be heard telling controllers shortly after, according to an audio recording posted online by Liveatc.net, a network that broadcasts live and archived air traffic control radio communications.The last transmission before the aircraft crashed into the ground was the pilot saying they were “out of time.” Weather at the nearby Palm Beach airport at the time of the crash indicated gusting winds, rain and low clouds.“You all saw what the weather was like here at the surface,” Chapman said. “What we have to determine is what the weather conditions were like at altitude.”The Learjet flew for approximately two hours after leaving Austin for the Bahamas and began its rapid descent around 12:48 p.m. local time on Sunday, according to preliminary data from Flightradar24. The data indicates the plane’s vertical descent rate eventually exceeded 32,000 feet per minute. Dashboard camera footage showed an almost vertical plunge before the impact and explosion alongside a highway.The NTSB said it was aware of one person on the ground who sustained a leg injury while driving a vehicle near the impact site.Chapman confirmed the aircraft was operated by Aurora Aviation Inc., doing business as Upper Jets. Attempts to reach representatives for Upper Jets were unsuccessful. The New York Times interviewed a woman, who said she was the mother of one of the pilots of the aircraft — a 20-year-old named Nathalia Filgueiras. According to the report, Filgueiras earned a pilot’s license at 17 and had logged more than 1,300 hours of flight time. A Threads account belonging to a Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras includes a post from March in which she’s posing from inside a Learjet 60, with the caption referencing her as pilot in command.Following the crash, some people took to social media to speculate about how the pilot’s unconfirmed age, race, gender or experience could have contributed to the accident.In a social media post to his personal X account, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman defended the pilot, writing that “she was doing her job, communicating with ATC right to the end in a terrifying situation.”Flight training is typically an arduous and costly process, with future pilots striving for a so-called type rating, an airframe-specific certification legally needed to fly any jet-powered aircraft. Though a pilot can earn initial qualification at the age of 17 in the US, completing the additional ratings and pre-requisites needed to earn their first type rating typically takes years.And even if candidates meet regulatory minimums, a hot job market for pilots has made jet aircraft careers fiercely competitive, with employers demanding even more hours and experience.Local first responders and officials declined to comment on the identity of any victims, and Tom Nadler, deputy county administrator for Palm Beach County, said there is DNA that needs to be matched before victims can be definitively identified. Officials said about 400 people had been displaced from near the crash site and the local government was working to temporarily relocate any impacted individuals. --With assistance from Matthew Griffin and Mathieu Dion.(Updates with additional air traffic audio from fourth paragraph and NASA administrator’s post in 14th paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
